newsitem.title: FIJI: RTRS-Greenpeace urges Fiji mine safeguards review.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Greenpeace urges Fiji mine safeguards review.

text.p: An independent assessment of environmental safeguards should be carried out at Pacific Island Gold NL's Mt Kasi mine following the sighting of dead fish in a local river, Greenpeace Pacific said on Monday.
The Fiji government said this week that some tailings and mill water escaped from the tailings dam after heavy rains and flowed into a tributary of the Yanawai River on the island of Vanua Levu.
The mine was closed voluntarily and operations would remain suspended until tailings and mill water were properly contained, the government said in a statement.

Pacific Islands chief executive Chris Adsett told Reuters about 30 dead fish were found this week by company officials at the mouth of the Yanawai River, some 12 km from the mine, during a regular patrol of local waterways.
It was the third time since June that small numbers of dead fish had been found, he said.
Adsett said the mine was able to release process water as part of its lease agreement, but the spill meant increased levels of solids would also have been released.
"Whether that caused the death of the fish some kilometres away we are not sure," he said.
The company hoped the mine, which had been closed for two or three days, would begin operations "in the not too distant future".
Greenpeace spokesman Dennis Rounds said in a statement that Fiji should urgently revise its Mining Act to ensure mining companies were responsible for any damage they caused to the environment.
Pacific Islands plans to produce 30,000 ounces of gold from Mt Kasi mine in 1996/97 after pouring its first gold in April. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
